minutes.headline: Sewer Commission found ~500 quarterly bills used stale 2022 rates, is sending corrective bills to recover ~$24,000
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Sewer Commission discussed recruiting for its vacant elected seat, approved prior minutes, and heard that a billing-system error reverted roughly half of quarterly bills to old 2022 rates, requiring a supplemental commitment and corrected bills to avoid losing about $24,000 in revenue. The commission also noted a new business-office assistant starting May 27, an update on planned manhole repairs, and set its meeting schedule through early July; no members of the public spoke.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept a regular and a supplemental billing commitment after a billing-system error reverted many quarterly bills to outdated 2022 rates.
A customer's unusually low bill first tipped off staff that accounts above the minimum charge were being billed at the wrong rate.
Corrective bills are going out to recover the underbilled revenue, with most per-account differences described as modest.
The commission agreed, without a formal vote, to send a revised recruitment letter for its vacant elected seat, reusing the prior water-customer mailing list.
A new business-office assistant starts May 27, and manhole-repair work is expected to begin in June.

why_it_matters: Customers billed above the minimum charge may receive a corrected bill reflecting current rates rather than the stale 2022 rate the system applied.
The sewer fund's revenue depends on those corrective bills going out and being paid, since the reverted rates undercharged a large share of accounts for a period.
The commission's elected seat stays vacant, leaving one fewer voice on rate and budget decisions until someone is recruited.
